vo.text:
Watch what a language model can do alone.
It cannot read your minutes. It cannot query Postgres. It is a text function.
Three assistants, four data sources. That is twelve private integrations. Twelve auth flows. Twelve schemas to keep current.

MCP replaces those private contracts with one public one. Three plus four is seven.
The lines got STANDARD, not shorter.
Separate three words people collapse. The host owns the model. The client holds one session. The server knows about neither.
A server exposes three things. Tools the model picks. Resources the application attaches. Prompts the user chooses deliberately.

Read that description field again. It is prompt engineering, not documentation.
It is the only instruction the model gets.

Every message is one JSON-RPC object. Look for the id.
A request carries one… a notification never does.
The handshake is three messages, and it is ordered. Initialize. Capabilities come back. Then initialized, and the session is live.

Now find the model in this loop. It is not on the wire.
It emits an intent, and the host does every translation.
Same messages, two pipes. Standard streams locally, HTTP everywhere else. On standard streams, stdout belongs to the protocol.

Keep two failures apart. A wrong method name is a protocol error.
A missing meeting is a result the model can recover from.

A valid token says who you are. It never says what you may read.
Make the user non-optional. The unscoped path stops existing.

Every byte you return is spent from the context window.
Return twenty of three hundred and forty matches… and say so.
